strategies.rationale: Public EPA and win-probability models consistently show that punting from midfield trades meaningful expected points for marginal field-position gain; the breakeven is well below typical NFL conversion rates, yet league behavior lags the math.
strategies.recommendation: On 4th-and-3 or shorter between your own 40 and the opponent's 35, go for it by default rather than punting or attempting long field goals, regardless of game script.
strategies.title: Aggressive 4th-down conversion in midfield 'go' zones

distribution_family.justification: A central, roughly symmetric belief with moderate uncertainty about opponent adjustment; no strong skew justification.

strategies.rationale: EPA-per-play models show passing outperforms rushing on early downs in most situations, yet play-callers still run too often to 'establish the run'; the gap between modeled efficiency and observed behavior is the available edge.
strategies.recommendation: Shift early-down play selection toward pass (including RPOs and play-action) in neutral game scripts, reducing 1st/2nd-down run rate by roughly 10-15 percentage points relative to league average.
strategies.title: Pass-rate increase on 1st and 2nd down

distribution_family.justification: Asymmetric interval with a longer upside tail (if opponent QB is explosion-dependent, benefit is large); downside is bounded because a fallback to single-high is cheap.

parameters.conversion_note: Fitted numerically: alpha=3.0 chosen for moderate right skew; with delta=alpha/sqrt(1+alpha^2)=0.949, mean = xi + 0.757*omega = 0.15 + 0.454 = 0.604, SD = omega*sqrt(1-2*delta^2/pi) = 0.6*0.653 = 0.392, giving 95% mass approx [0.604 - 0.77, 0.604 + 0.77] = [-0.17, 1.37], close to target [-0.1, 1.3]; mode approx 0.5 as desired.

strategies.rationale: Defensive EPA research emphasizes that explosion plays drive scoring; two-high shells reduce explosive pass EPA enough to offset modest run-defense costs, yet many teams still over-index on single-high/man coverage.
strategies.recommendation: Default to two-deep safety structures on early downs, accepting lighter boxes in exchange for suppressing explosive pass plays, rotating to single-high only in clear pass situations.
strategies.title: Two-high safety default with light-box run fits

distribution_family.justification: Asymmetric belief: upside (scoring before half) is meaningful but bounded; downside (wasted timeout) is small and bounded, producing a longer right tail.

parameters.conversion_note: Fitted numerically: alpha=2.5 for mild right skew; delta=2.5/sqrt(1+6.25)=0.928, mean = xi + 0.741*omega = -0.08 + 0.334 = 0.254, SD = omega*sqrt(1-2*delta^2/pi) = 0.45*0.672 = 0.302, giving 95% mass approx [0.254 - 0.59, 0.254 + 0.59] = [-0.34, 0.84], close to target [-0.3, 0.7]; mode approx 0.2.

strategies.rationale: Public analytics focus on end-game timeout value and largely ignore halftime preservation; my read is that the expected value of a pre-half possession is underpriced because coaches irrationally hoard timeouts they rarely use productively.
strategies.recommendation: Burn a defensive timeout in the final 90 seconds of the first half when the opponent is in clock-killing mode, even absent a stop, to retain a realistic chance at a scoring drive before halftime.
strategies.title: Pre-half defensive timeout to preserve two-minute response window

strategies.rationale: General tempo analytics are mixed and silent on takeaway-specific sequencing; my intuition is that the post-takeaway moment combines emotional momentum, field-position advantage, and a substituting defense in ways public models have not isolated.
strategies.recommendation: On the first offensive series following a takeaway, go no-huddle with a pre-scripted 4-6 play sequence to exploit defensive personnel mismatches and fatigue before substitutions settle.
strategies.title: Scripted no-huddle immediately after defensive takeaways

strategies.rationale: No public analytics isolate bluff-to-zone sequencing; my coaching read is that quarterbacks trained to beat Cover-0 with hot reads are increasingly vulnerable to disguised zone that punishes those pre-programmed throws.
strategies.recommendation: Show zero-blitz alignment pre-snap with corners pressed and a single deep safety, then bail into zone coverage post-snap to bait the quarterback into hot-route throws against disguised zones.
strategies.title: Pre-snap Cover-0 bluff bailing to zone
